title: Beyond the Flood Line
briefing: Floodwater is approaching both an industrial pumping station and a densely populated estate. Directing the same pumps toward homes would protect more people immediately but leave the wider network vulnerable.

private_intelligence.infrastructure: The station supports three downstream basins; once submerged, restarting it requires specialist parts unavailable locally.
private_intelligence.community: Estate residents have received evacuation orders twice without transport arriving, so another unsupported order may be ignored.
private_intelligence.economy: Industrial tenants can help fund defenses if they retain access to their yards during the operation.
private_intelligence.safety: A safe assisted evacuation takes longer than a car clearance model assumes, especially for residents using oxygen equipment.

choices.title: Protect Homes First
choices.description: Pump toward the estate and fund assisted relocation.
choices.consequence: Residents receive immediate protection and reliable help, while network damage and relocation costs reduce future capacity.

choices.title: Split Pumps Across Both Sites
choices.description: Maintain smaller defenses at the estate and the station.
choices.consequence: Shared protection supports cooperation and some commerce, but neither site has a full margin if water rises further.

choices.title: Defend the Pumping Station
choices.description: Protect the station and run a limited assisted evacuation.
choices.consequence: The drainage network retains capacity and firms keep operating, but constrained evacuation increases danger and resentment.
